label: Dashboard / admin panel
summary: Data-heavy screens: KPIs, charts, tables, filters and roles

options.question: Are there different roles or permission views (for example admin and viewer)?

preview_screen: The overview page: a KPI row, one main chart, and a table with realistic numbers and a filter bar.
code_target: An app in the project's stack (plain HTML, CSS and JS by default) with a sidebar or top-nav shell, working filters, tables and charts (an accessible charting library or hand-built SVG), mock data.
required_screens: Detail view for a table row
required_states: Empty state for charts and tables (no data yet)
Loading skeletons shaped like the charts
Error state per widget with retry
Table row selected and bulk action bar
design_guidance: Raise data-ink ratio: remove needless gridlines, 3D effects and shadows; let the data speak.
Colour encodes meaning (up/down, category, time), never decoration. Don't use colour alone for status.
Numbers are right-aligned in tables, use tabular figures, and show units.
Use realistic, uneven values (47.2%, 1,284) and not round placeholders.
Each widget has its own title, time range and loading/error state.

checks: Every chart has a title, labelled axes or direct labels, units, and a legend or direct labels that don't rely on colour alone.
Chart series colours stay distinguishable at 3:1 against the background and against each other, and still work for common colour-blindness.
Table columns align by type (numbers right, text left) and long values truncate with a way to read the full text.
Every widget has loading, empty and error states, and filters have a no-results state.
A visible scope is shown for filtered data (date range, segment) so users know what they are looking at.
